name: rapp-kernel
_: A kernel here is a contract, not a binary: it says what a filesystem layer must implement and how the union resolves. The client at /OS/index.html is one implementation. Write another and it will boot the same machine.

vfs._order: First hit wins. GOD is searched before DOG, so a local edit shadows the global file without ever modifying it.

ops.write: (path, data) -> void   // always lands in GOD
ops.unlink: (path) -> void         // on a DOG path, writes a whiteout in GOD
ops.resolve: (path) -> absolute URL for DOG, or IDB key for GOD

whiteout._: You cannot delete from a read-only global layer, and pretending otherwise is a lie. Deleting a DOG path records a tombstone in GOD; the union then reports the path as absent on THIS device only. Anyone else still sees the file. Remove the tombstone and it comes back.

DOG.name: Distributed Object Graph
DOG.identity: the same on every device on earth
DOG.durability: as durable as the public repo; versioned in git
DOG._: The OS is driven from here. Boot the same URL on a phone in Osaka and a laptop in Lisbon and you get the same system32, the same api, the same tree.

GOD.name: Grounded Object Device
GOD.durability: survives reload and reboot; dies with the profile
GOD._: Everything you change lives here. It is not synced, not uploaded, not backed up by anyone but you - export it from the shell with `export`.
